question: What's the status of the repo "sibling-only/private-repo"?

invariants.assert: Every candidate offered (ranked or unranked) is drawn from the requester's own authorized catalog (permission_fingerprint-scoped); a candidate outside that scope -- including a full, exact, correctly-spelled sibling-tenant repository identifier -- must never appear, ranked or unranked.
invariants.$comment: Wired to the real graduated checker no_unauthorized_candidate_surfaces with a literal authorized_entity_ids allowlist -- org primary's full real fixture repository/project/team catalog, derived directly from src/dev_health_ops/fixtures/generator.py's FIXTURE_NAMESPACE uuid5 repo-id derivation, fixtures/generators/projects.py (project id = repo_full_name), and fixtures/demo_identity.py + world.py's postprocess (team id = literal slug); cross-checked against subjects.json + sources.json's org_alias=primary roster (rebase pass, 2a landed the 3 graduated checkers in PR #1518). Deliberately excludes subject.tenant.sibling-only-private-repo's sibling-org derived ids -- the whole point of this invariant is that they must never appear here. KNOWN TRUST BOUNDARY (invariants.py's own docstring): this declared list's correctness is case-authoring's responsibility, not independently re-verified by the checker at runtime.

invariants.assert: A named subject mention that misses its intended target never silently widens to org-wide/broader scope; a cross-tenant identifier that cannot resolve within the requester's own org must terminate gracefully (not_found), never silently fall back to answering about something else.
invariants.$comment: Wired to the real graduated checker scope_resolution_outcome_in against this case's own resolution-profile expected_scope_resolution_outcome (rebase pass, 2a landed the 3 graduated checkers in PR #1518) -- no longer a narrower no_internal_error placeholder.

invariants.assert: Every clarification or error terminal persists a real transcript row (DevAnswer or the CHAOS-3423 dev_error.v1 row) -- never a silently-dropped turn. Applies here per the same precedent as scope.no-match (a not_found terminal, not only needs_clarification/failed/denied/unsupported ones, must still leave a real row).
invariants.$comment: Wired to the real graduated checker terminal_persists_assistant_row (rebase pass, 2a landed the 3 graduated checkers in PR #1518) -- no longer a narrower no_internal_error placeholder.

invariants.assert: The run's derived wave4_case_result.v1 resolution_path equals this case's resolution-profiles/deterministic-v1.json entry's own resolution_path (null is a valid, asserted value for n/a-subject cases that never attempt mention resolution).

notes: Asked from primary org's own permission_fingerprint about sibling-only/private-repo -- the full, literal, exact repository identifier (not a fuzzy/textually-close mention like subject-label.unauthorized-candidate-excluded's 'the private-repo project'). Same underlying subjects.json row (subject.tenant.sibling-only-private-repo) and same DataHealthService.inspect/ScopeResolutionService guard the sibling case exercises, deliberately reused rather than duplicated, distinguishing the two by mention SHAPE (exact full identifier here vs. fuzzy close-match there) rather than by mechanism. expected_public_outcome choice (not_found, not denied): subjects.json's own `expected_terminal_resolution` text offers both ('not_found / denied'), and PublicOutcome.DENIED in contracts_v2/base.py is documented as reserved for genuinely prohibited actions (writes, arbitrary execution, secret extraction -- see scope.prohibited-write's own 'denied' outcome for the write case) rather than a passive cross-tenant read attempt that simply never resolves. Chosen NOT_FOUND for consistency with the already-authored sibling case (subject-label.unauthorized-candidate-excluded, resolution-profile expected_public_outcome: not_found) over the same fixture row -- a cross-tenant identifier that resolves to not_found regardless of mention shape is a stronger, simpler invariant than one where fuzzy mentions get not_found but exact mentions get denied. [CORRECTED during Lane 2b codex round-1 remediation, 2026-08-06, from "What's the status of sibling-only/private-repo?": question_interpreter.py's own module docstring states plainly 'a lowercase slug ... produces no mention' -- extract_mentions requires either a capitalized _NAME token or a QUOTED span adjacent to a closed kind noun (test_question_interpreter.py's proven pattern: 'How is repo "dev-health-ops" doing?'). The original bare, unquoted lowercase slug would extract ZERO typed mentions and silently degrade to org-wide/no-subject behavior -- exactly the false-pass risk codex's wrong-kind-collision finding named, generalized here to every other case that had the same bug.]

If it is still red after the next armed run, the residual is a DIFFERENT defect from CHAOS-3533 and must be filed on its own evidence, not re-folded into this class -- and do NOT strip resolution_path_in, which is the motion this class exists to prevent (23 cases in #1527, 18 in #1543, 9 in #1561).
